title: NBA roster transaction legality under the 2023 CBA
description: Research encoding of the Collective Bargaining Agreement excerpt distributed with the RuleArena NBA benchmark, for study 001 (policy representation). The pack decides whether a set of roster operations is legal. It contains no arithmetic: JPS 0.1.0-draft compares facts only, so every derived quantity is read from /facts/derived/* and is produced by a separate published deterministic preprocessor. See packs/COVERAGE.md for scope, the exact derived-field contract, and the numbered readings taken where the CBA text was ambiguous.

decision.intent: Determine whether a proposed set of NBA roster operations is legal under the encoded provisions of the Collective Bargaining Agreement, or must be escalated because a fact the encoded provisions depend on is unavailable.
decision.question: Is this set of NBA roster operations legal under the CBA?

evidenceRequirements.description: The executed Player Contract, Offer Sheet, or trade call for every operation under test, including term, first-year Salary, Unlikely Bonuses, and the Exception invoked.
The published deterministic computation of each team's Team Salary, Room, cap holds, Salary Cap, First Apron Level, and Second Apron Level immediately before and after each operation.
Each player's Years of Service, free-agency class under Article I, age, and Higher Max Criteria record.

outcomes.label: Legal
outcomes.description: No encoded CBA provision is violated on the facts supplied. This is the pack's fallback outcome: it is reached only when every rule evaluated to false, so it is never reached while any needed fact is unknown.

outcomes.label: Illegal
outcomes.description: At least one encoded CBA provision is violated. Every rule in this pack is a violation detector and resolves to this outcome, so multiple simultaneous violations agree rather than conflict.

rules.description: A team whose transaction uses no Section 6 Exception may not end that transaction with a Team Salary above the Salary Cap.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 2(b)(1): a Team's Team Salary may not exceed the Salary Cap at any time unless the Team is using one of the Section 6 Exceptions.

rules.description: A new Contract for a player with fewer than seven Years of Service may not exceed the greater of 25% of the Salary Cap and 105% of his prior Salary (30% for a 5th Year Eligible Player who met a Higher Max Criterion).
rules.rationale: Article II, Section 7(a)(i): the greater of 25% of the Salary Cap or 105% of the prior Season's Salary, raised to 30% for a 5th Year Eligible Player re-signing with his Prior Team who met a Higher Max Criterion.

rules.description: A new Contract for a player with at least seven but fewer than ten Years of Service may not exceed the greater of 30% of the Salary Cap and 105% of his prior Salary (35% under a Designated Veteran Player Contract).
rules.rationale: Article II, Section 7(a)(ii): the greater of 30% of the Salary Cap or 105% of the prior Season's Salary, raised to 35% for an eligible Designated Veteran Player Contract with the Prior Team.

rules.description: A new Contract for a player with ten or more Years of Service may not exceed the greater of 35% of the Salary Cap and 105% of his prior Salary.
rules.rationale: Article II, Section 7(a)(iii): the greater of 35% of the Salary Cap or 105% of the prior Season's Salary.

rules.description: A 5th Year Eligible Player who met no Higher Max Criterion is capped at 25% of the Salary Cap, and any 5th Year Eligible Contract above 25% must cover at least four Seasons.
rules.rationale: Article II, Section 7(a)(i)(A)-(B) defines the Higher Max Criteria that unlock 30%; Section 7(g) requires at least four Seasons for any 5th Year Eligible Contract above 25% of the Salary Cap.

rules.description: Annual Salary changes in a Contract between a Qualifying or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent and his Prior Team may not exceed 8% of the first-year Salary.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 5(a)(2)(i): no more than eight percent (8%) of the Salary for the first Salary Cap Year covered by the Contract.

rules.description: Same provision as the preceding rule under the benchmark's alternate annotation spelling: the 8% annual change limit for Qualifying and Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agents re-signing with their Prior Team.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 5(a)(2)(i). Encoded twice because the benchmark's citation vocabulary contains two spellings of the same provision.

rules.description: Annual Salary changes in every other Player Contract may not exceed 5% of the first-year Salary.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 5(a)(1)(i): no more than five percent (5%) of the Salary for the first Salary Cap Year covered by the Contract.

rules.description: A Player Contract may cover no more than four Seasons, or five Seasons between a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent and his Prior Team.
rules.rationale: Article IX: up to but no more than four (4) Seasons; five (5) Seasons for a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent and his Prior Team. Lengths are inclusive of any Option Year.

rules.description: A Contract signed under the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may not exceed four Seasons.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(e)(2): the term may not exceed four (4) Seasons in length.

rules.description: A Contract signed under the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may not exceed two Seasons.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(f)(1): Contracts not to exceed two (2) Seasons in length.

rules.description: A Contract signed under the Bi-annual Exception may not exceed two Seasons.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(d)(2): the term may not exceed two (2) Seasons in length.

rules.description: A Contract signed under the Mid-Level Salary Exception for Room Teams may not exceed three Seasons.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(g)(2): the term may not exceed three (3) Seasons in length.

rules.description: A Contract signed under the Minimum Player Salary Exception may not exceed two Seasons.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(i): a Player Contract not to exceed two (2) Seasons in length.

rules.description: The Qualifying Veteran Free Agent Exception is available only to a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent re-signing with his Prior Team, and only up to the Article II, Section 7 maximum.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(b)(1) read with Article I(yy): the player must be a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent contracting with his Prior Team, and the Contract may provide up to the maximum in Article II, Section 7.

rules.description: Same provision as the preceding rule under the benchmark's alternate annotation spelling (“qualified” rather than “qualifying”).
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(b)(1). Encoded twice because the benchmark's citation vocabulary contains two spellings of the same provision.

rules.description: The Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent Exception requires an eligible player and Prior Team, a term of at least two Seasons, and a first-year amount no greater than 175% of prior Salary or 105% of the Average Player Salary.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(b)(3)(i) read with Article I(t): the new Contract must cover at least two (2) Seasons and may provide up to the greater of 175% of the prior Regular Salary or 105% of the Average Player Salary for the prior Salary Cap Year.

rules.description: The Non-Qualifying Veteran Free Agent Exception permits at most the greater of 120% of prior Regular Salary and 120% of the applicable Minimum Annual Salary.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(b)(2) read with Article I(rr): the greater of 120% of the final-year Regular Salary or 120% of the then-current Minimum Annual Salary applicable to the player.

rules.description: Contracts signed or acquired under the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may total at most 9.12% of the Salary Cap in the first Salary Cap Year.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(e)(1): in the aggregate up to 9.12% of the Salary Cap for such Salary Cap Year.

rules.description: Same provision as the preceding rule under the benchmark's alternate annotation spelling (“nontaxpayer” rather than “non_taxpayer”).
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(e)(1). Encoded twice because the benchmark's citation vocabulary contains two spellings of the same provision.

rules.description: Contracts signed under the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may total at most the Taxpayer Mid-Level amount, and the exception is available only if the team's Team Salary immediately afterwards exceeds the First Apron Level.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(f)(1): up to $5 million scaled by the Salary Cap ratio to 2023-24, “provided that the Team's Team Salary immediately following the Team's use of such Exception exceeds the First Apron Level”.

rules.description: Contracts signed or acquired under the Mid-Level Salary Exception for Room Teams may total at most 5.678% of the Salary Cap in the first Salary Cap Year.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(g)(1): in the aggregate up to 5.678% of the Salary Cap for such Salary Cap Year.

rules.description: Contracts signed or acquired under the Bi-annual Exception may total at most 3.32% of the Salary Cap in the first Salary Cap Year.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(d)(1): in the aggregate up to 3.32% of the Salary Cap for such Salary Cap Year.

rules.description: A Contract signed under the Minimum Player Salary Exception must provide exactly the applicable Minimum Player Salary for the first Season, with no bonuses of any kind.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(i): a Salary for the first Season equal to the Minimum Player Salary applicable to that player (with no bonuses of any kind).

rules.description: A team that signs or acquires a player using the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may not have a Team Salary above the First Apron Level.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 2(e)(2)(i) with Transaction Restrictions Table row B: Applicable Apron Level is the First Apron Level.

rules.description: Same provision as the preceding rule under the benchmark's alternate annotation spelling.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 2(e)(2)(i), table row B. Encoded twice because the benchmark's citation vocabulary contains two spellings of the same provision.

rules.description: A team deemed to have used the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception instead of the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may not have a Team Salary above the Second Apron Level.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(f)(5): the Team “will be deemed to have used the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception instead of the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception for all purposes under this Article VII”, which carries the row K Second Apron Level restriction. See COVERAGE decision 6.

rules.description: A team that signs a player using the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may not have a Team Salary above the Second Apron Level.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 2(e)(2)(i) with Transaction Restrictions Table row K: Applicable Apron Level is the Second Apron Level.

rules.description: A team that has already signed a Contract using the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception in the Salary Cap Year may not engage in any of the First-Apron-restricted transactions in rows A through F of the Transaction Restrictions Table.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 2(e)(2)(iii)(B): a Team may not engage in any transaction set forth in rows A through F if it has previously signed a Player Contract pursuant to the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception during such Salary Cap Year. See COVERAGE decision 7.

rules.description: A team that signs or acquires a player using the Bi-annual Exception may not have a Team Salary above the First Apron Level.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 2(e)(2)(i) with Transaction Restrictions Table row A: Applicable Apron Level is the First Apron Level.

rules.description: Replacement Player salaries acquired under the Standard Traded Player Exception may exceed 100% of the Traded Player's pre-trade Salary by no more than $250,000.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(j)(1)(i): no more than one hundred percent (100%) of the pre-trade Salary of the Traded Player, plus $250,000.

rules.description: Replacement Player salaries acquired under the Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception may exceed 100% of the aggregated pre-trade Salaries by no more than $250,000.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(j)(1)(ii): no more than one hundred percent (100%) of the aggregated pre-trade Salaries of the Traded Players, plus $250,000.

rules.description: Replacement Player salaries acquired under the Expanded Traded Player Exception may not exceed the greater of 125% of outgoing salary plus $250,000 and the lesser of 200% plus $250,000 or 100% plus the scaled $7.5 million allowance.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(j)(1)(iv): the greater of (y) the lesser of 200% plus $250,000 or 100% plus $7.5 million scaled by the Salary Cap ratio to 2023-24, or (z) 125% plus $250,000.

rules.description: A team below the Salary Cap acquiring players by assignment may take back no more than its Room plus $250,000.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(j)(1)(v): post-assignment Salaries in the aggregate no more than the Team's room under the Salary Cap plus $250,000.

rules.description: The $250,000 allowance in every Traded Player Exception is reduced to $0 when the team's post-assignment Team Salary would exceed the First Apron Level.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(j)(3): if a Team's post-assignment Team Salary would exceed the First Apron Level, the $250,000 allowance referenced in Sections 6(j)(1)(i)-(v) is reduced to $0.

rules.description: When three or more Contracts are aggregated outside the December 15 to trade-deadline window and fewer Replacement Players are acquired than are traded, at most one Traded Player may be a Minimum Traded Player.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(j)(4)(ii): other than from December 15 through the trade deadline, if a Team aggregates three or more Traded Players and acquires fewer Replacement Players, no more than one of those Traded Players may be a Minimum Traded Player.

rules.description: A team that acquires a player using an Expanded Traded Player Exception may not have a Team Salary above the First Apron Level.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 2(e)(2)(i) with Transaction Restrictions Table row E: Applicable Apron Level is the First Apron Level.

rules.description: A team that acquires a player using an Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception may not have a Team Salary above the Second Apron Level.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 2(e)(2)(i) with Transaction Restrictions Table row H: Applicable Apron Level is the Second Apron Level.

rules.description: A Contract signed and traded under Section 8(e)(1) must cover at least three and no more than four Seasons, excluding any Option Year.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 8(e)(1)(ii): the Contract is for at least three (3) Seasons (excluding any Option Year) but no more than four (4) Seasons in length.

rules.description: A Contract signed and traded under Section 8(e)(1) may not be signed pursuant to the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception or the Mid-Level Salary Exception for Room Teams.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 8(e)(1)(iii): the Contract is not signed pursuant to the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception or the Mid-Level Salary Exception for Room Teams.

rules.description: The acquiring team in a Section 8(e)(1) sign-and-trade must have Room for the first-Season Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 8(e)(1)(vii): the acquiring Team has Room for the player's Salary plus any Unlikely Bonuses provided for in the first Season of the Contract.

rules.description: A Section 8(e)(1) Contract for a 5th Year Eligible Player who met a Higher Max Criterion may not exceed 25% of the Salary Cap.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 8(e)(1)(vi): for a 5th Year Eligible Player who met one of the Higher Max Criteria, the Contract may not provide Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses in excess of 25% of the Salary Cap.

rules.description: A team that acquires a player under a Contract entered into pursuant to Section 8(e)(1) may not have a Team Salary above the First Apron Level.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 2(e)(2)(i) with Transaction Restrictions Table row C: Applicable Apron Level is the First Apron Level.

rules.description: When a Qualifying or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent signs above the Non-Qualifying amount with an over-the-cap Prior Team and is immediately traded, the assignor's Traded Player Exception is computed from the deemed salary, and incoming salary above that deemed limit plus $250,000 is not permitted.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 6(j)(5): the player's Salary shall be deemed equal to the greater of the Salary for the last Season of his preceding Contract or fifty percent (50%) of the Salary for the first Season of his new Contract.

rules.description: A team that acquires a player using a Traded Player Exception arising from a Contract signed and traded under Section 8(e)(1) may not have a Team Salary above the Second Apron Level.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 2(e)(2)(i) with Transaction Restrictions Table row J: Applicable Apron Level is the Second Apron Level.

rules.description: A team may pay or receive at most 5.15% of the Salary Cap in cash across all trades in a Salary Cap Year, without netting.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 8(a): up to an aggregate amount equal to 5.15% of the Salary Cap for such Salary Cap Year in cash across all such trades; amounts paid and received are not netted.

rules.description: A team that pays cash to another team in connection with a trade may not have a Team Salary above the Second Apron Level.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 2(e)(2)(i) with Transaction Restrictions Table row I: Applicable Apron Level is the Second Apron Level.

rules.description: A team may not sell a first round draft pick for cash, nor trade a first round pick if the result may leave it without first-round picks in two consecutive future Drafts.
rules.rationale: By-Laws, Section 7.03: no Team may sell its first round selection rights for cash or its equivalent, or trade them if the result may be to leave the Team without first-round picks in any two consecutive future NBA Drafts.

rules.description: A team may not trade a first round pick if the result may leave it without first-round picks in two consecutive future Drafts.
rules.rationale: By-Laws, Section 7.03, consecutive-Drafts limb only. Encoded separately because the benchmark's citation vocabulary names the combined and the consecutive-only formulations distinctly.

rules.description: A Standard NBA Contract signed by a Free Agent may not be traded before the later of three months after signing and December 15 of that Salary Cap Year.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 8(d)(ii): no player who signs a Standard NBA Contract as a Free Agent may be traded before the later of three (3) months following signing or the December 15 of the Salary Cap Year in which the Contract was signed; the rule does not apply to the initial trade of a Contract signed under Section 8(e).

rules.description: Salaries in an Over 38 Contract are re-attributed to earlier Salary Cap Years, and a signing is illegal when the re-attributed Team Salary, and only the re-attributed Team Salary, exceeds the Salary Cap.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 3(a)(2)(i): aggregate Salaries from the later of the fourth Salary Cap Year or the first Salary Cap Year following the player's 38th birthday are attributed pro rata to prior Salary Cap Years. See COVERAGE decision 9.

rules.description: For a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent aged 35 or 36 signing a five-Season Over 38 Contract with his Prior Team, only the fifth-year Salary is re-attributed; the signing is illegal when that re-attribution, and only that re-attribution, puts the team over the Salary Cap.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 3(a)(2)(ii) and (iv): the fifth Salary Cap Year is re-attributed for a five-Season Contract, and there is no re-allocation at all for a Contract covering four or fewer Seasons entered into at age 35 or 36. See COVERAGE decision 9.

rules.description: Same provision as the preceding rule under the benchmark's alternate annotation spelling.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 3(a)(2)(ii). Encoded twice because the benchmark's citation vocabulary contains two spellings of the same provision.

rules.description: A Qualifying Veteran Free Agent's Free Agent Amount stays in his Prior Team's Team Salary until he re-signs, signs elsewhere, or is renounced; the transaction is illegal when that hold, and only that hold, puts the team over the Salary Cap.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 4(d)(1): 150% of prior Salary (190% if below the Estimated Average Player Salary; 250%/300% after a second Option Year), capped by 4(d)(5). See COVERAGE decision 8.

rules.description: An Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent's Free Agent Amount stays in his Prior Team's Team Salary; the transaction is illegal when that hold, and only that hold, puts the team over the Salary Cap.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 4(d)(2): 130% of prior Salary unless the Prior Team renounces its Early Qualifying rights. See COVERAGE decision 8.

rules.description: A Non-Qualifying Veteran Free Agent's Free Agent Amount stays in his Prior Team's Team Salary; the transaction is illegal when that hold, and only that hold, puts the team over the Salary Cap.
rules.rationale: Article VII, Section 4(d)(3): 120% of prior Salary. See COVERAGE decision 8.

rules.description: An Offer Sheet to a Restricted Free Agent with one or two Years of Service may not provide first- or second-year Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses above the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level amount.
rules.rationale: Article XI, Section 5(d)(i): no such Offer Sheet may provide for Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses in the first Salary Cap Year totaling more than the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception amount, with the second year bounded by Article VII, Section 5(a)(1). See COVERAGE decision 10.

rules.description: When the first two Salary Cap Years of such an Offer Sheet are at the maximum allowable amount, the third year may not exceed the maximum the player could have received absent the Section 5(d)(i) restriction.
rules.rationale: Article XI, Section 5(d)(ii), first sentence.

rules.description: When such an Offer Sheet uses the third-year maximum, the fourth year may change by no more than 4.5% of the third year's Salary.
rules.rationale: Article XI, Section 5(d)(ii)(A): the player's Salary for the fourth Salary Cap Year may increase or decrease in relation to the third Salary Cap Year's Salary by no more than 4.5% of the Salary for the third Salary Cap Year.

rules.description: Same provision as the preceding rule under the benchmark's alternate annotation spelling.
rules.rationale: Article XI, Section 5(d)(ii)(A). Encoded twice because the benchmark's citation vocabulary contains two spellings of the same provision.

rules.description: For an Offer Sheet extended under Section 5(d)(ii), which necessarily covers more than two Salary Cap Years, the New Team must have Room for the average of the aggregate Salaries.
rules.rationale: Article XI, Section 5(d)(iii) read with 5(b): the Salary for the first Salary Cap Year is deemed to equal the average of the aggregate Salaries for each Salary Cap Year covered by the Offer Sheet, and the New Team must have Room for it. See COVERAGE decision 11.

exceptions.description: The instance turns on a CBA provision family that this pack does not encode (listed in packs/COVERAGE.md, section 'Out of scope'). No legality answer may be produced from the encoded rules alone.

escalation.message: A fact that an encoded CBA provision depends on is unavailable, or the instance turns on a provision this pack does not encode. Review the trace: each unknown rule names the /facts/derived/* pointer it could not resolve, and each rule's sourceRefs name the CBA section to consult.
